answer: A practical Sybil defense is a bond-and-delay gate. Each identity must lock stake frozen while a probe inspects its history, so a clone ring duplicates capital per head instead of reusing it, and that capital earns nothing, like water trapped in a karst aquifer. Misbehaviour slashes the lock, so it cannot be recycled into a fresh name; trust weight accrues only with age, which a ring cannot forge, and dormant clones pay demurrage, so a large onyx ledger becomes a liability. The attacker pays many times the join price plus frozen funds and repeated slashes.
